transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Start: 2026-05-22T15:00:00Z
Duration: 52 minutes (call lasted ~52m)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Jared Stone (Cobalt CTO), Priya Rao (Cobalt Head of ML), Leo Martin (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): POC to run transaction enrichment at scale. Focus on QPS/concurrency, input/output token distributions, latency SLOs, dataset/sample traffic, security checklist and pilot timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll run through the scope for the POC and do some workload modeling, quick intros?
[00:06] Jared: Jared Stone here, CTO at Cobalt, we run the payment routing and enrichment stack, Priya's here for the ML side, Leo for infra.
[00:12] Priya: hi all.
[00:13] Ravi: Ravi Patel, SE on Redwood, I'll drive benchmarks and the harness during the POC.
[00:18] Leo: Leo Martin, infra.
[00:20] Maya: great, quick agenda: success criteria, traffic characterization, benchmark plan, timeline and security. sound good?
[00:25] Jared: yep

[00:30] Priya: first, our main use-case: real-time transaction enrichment and risk scoring. we call an LLM to normalize merchant names, extract context, and generate risk tags. typically part of our synchronous path, budgeted for about 100-200ms p95 ideally, but we'll see.
[00:46] Ravi: ok that's helpful, given synchronous path we need low latency. can you give current traffic? qps, burst, average payload size?
[00:54] Priya: on average we see 15 QPS; peak is around 60 QPS during batch windows. about 10k transactions per hour on some days. most requests are short, like 10-40 tokens, but we also batch larger doc extraction for merchant profiles (500-1k tokens) in async flows.
[01:13] Maya: useful. for modelling POC let's split into three buckets: short conversational-ish queries (10-50 tokens) ~65% of traffic, medium context (150-300 tokens) ~25%, long profile requests (500-1200 tokens) ~10%. output token distribution roughly 8-20 tokens for short, 30-80 tokens for medium, 200-400 tokens for long. does that map to your data?
[01:36] Priya: yea that's a good approximation. our main SLO is p95 latency under 200ms for the short path, and p95 under 800ms for medium. long jobs are async so throughput matters more than p95.
[01:48] Ravi: ok from Redwood side we recommend testing with both hosted and Dedicated variants. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and easier KV-cache pinning for repeated merchant context. hosted is faster to start but you can see more latency variance.
[02:02] Leo: for Dedicated we'll need to validate VPC peering and egress rules. also KMS integration for keys.
[02:09] Maya: noted. on security: we do SOC2, can support KMS/HSM integrations and fine-grained RBAC. we'll share the security packet.

[02:20] Jared: timeline wise we want to run a 3-week pilot benchmark then a month-long performance validation before a production rollout. does that align with Redwood's typical POC?
[02:31] Maya: yes, that's typical: week 0 onboarding and dataset ingestion, week 1 bench runs and tuning, week 2 stress and end-to-end integration, week 3 sign-off and contract for Dedicated if desired.
[02:44] Priya: for success criteria, we'll measure: 1) p95 latency for short path < 200ms, 2) cost per 1k transactions below our target (we gave ballpark) 3) correctness baseline on our prompt evals (F1-like metrics for extraction).
[02:59] Ravi: also we'll surface tokens/op cost and tail-latency for concurrency > 20. we'll run concurrency sweeps to locate sweet spot for batching vs latency.

[03:10] Priya: what's concurrency and batching behavior we should expect? typical concurrency on our side is around 40 concurrent requests during peak, but most spread across service nodes.
[03:20] Ravi: ok we should model both QPS and concurrency. recommended pilot config: simulate 60 QPS burst for 30s, steady 18 QPS, concurrency tests at 10, 20, 40, 80. model input token distributions I noted earlier. we'll include cold-starts and warmed KV-cache runs.
[03:38] Jared: what's KV cache, sorry? sometimes people say K-V cash in notes, ha.
[03:42] Maya: KV cache, key-value cache for past tokens/state, helps with repeated merchant prompts, reduces compute and latency when context repeats.
[03:49] Leo: we have repeated merchant ids, so that would help. how are you measuring cost? tokens in/out?
[03:55] Ravi: cost units are tokens in + tokens out; for Dedicated we can provide per-node throughput and expected tokens/sec. we'll run benchmark harness to report tokens/sec, latency percentiles, and GPU utilization.

[04:08] Priya: our prompt mix: the short normalization prompt is the most common, typical input 25 tokens, output 12 tokens. medium enrichment ~220 tokens in, 60 out. long profile generation 900 in, 300 out. we can provide sample CSV with tokenized lengths.
[04:25] Maya: perfect, please share sample CSV. Priya: will do.

[04:28] Jared: what about quantization and model variants? we want to use an open model with similar quality to proprietary ones for cost reasons.
[04:36] Ravi: we can run small-benchmarks on a few variants. quantized models (like 4-bit) reduce GPU memory and increase throughput but sometimes add latency variance; we recommend trying both int8/4-bit variants in a smoke test. also multi-model fallbacks: if Dedicated capacity full we can fallback to hosted for non-sensitive payloads.
[04:55] Leo: data residency and encryption: all data in flight TLS, at rest encrypted. KMS integration for customer-managed keys is supported?
[05:03] Maya: yes we support customer-managed KMS and can document HSM options. we'll provide SOC2 and network diagrams.

[05:12] Priya: practical question: how long does it take to run a representative benchmark for us? we want statistically significant p95 numbers across the token distribution.
[05:21] Ravi: plan for 2-4 hours for an initial sweep per config (model + quant), then longer stress runs overnight to pick up tail behavior. for p95 stable numbers across buckets maybe 30-60 minutes per bucket at steady-state.

[05:36] Jared: ok costs: rough expectations?
[05:38] Maya: we'll send a price estimate. ballpark for Dedicated depends on GPU type and cluster size; for your expected 60 QPS peak with 65% short tokens we estimate needing N GPUs (we'll give exact after model selection and test runs). we'll include cost per 1k transactions for hosted vs Dedicated.

[05:55] Priya: measurement plan: we want these artefacts from Redwood: benchmark harness + scripts, measurement dashboard, and suggested prompt tuning. also we want to run correctness evals using our golden sets.
[06:06] Ravi: yes we'll share harness (Jenkins/curl-based and a k6 scenario), sample datasets, and a metrics dashboard with traces. we'll also include how batching and KV-cache settings were set for each run.

[06:19] Leo: networking: for Dedicated POC we'll likely want VPC peering and private endpoints. can you support SAML SSO for console?
[06:27] Maya: yes SAML/SSO is supported and we can provide onboarding docs.

[06:31] Maya: any blockers from your side right now?
[06:33] Priya: just getting sample traffic together and internal approvals for sending anonymized logs.

[06:37] Jared: also need to loop in security and legal for KMS/contract.

[06:41] Maya: ok to recap next steps - Redwood to send price estimate and security packet; SE to share benchmark harness; customer to send sample traffic and success criteria doc; schedule kickoff. owners and dates noted in action items.

[06:55] Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone.

[06:58] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up via email with links to docs and the benchmark repo.

[07:05] (call end)

Notes on modelling parameters agreed:
- Baseline steady-state QPS: 18 QPS (expected average)
- Peak burst QPS: 60 QPS for 30-120s windows
- Concurrency points to test: 10, 20, 40, 80
- Input token distribution: short (10-50 tokens) 65%, medium (150-300) 25%, long (500-1200) 10%
- Output token distribution: short 8-20, medium 30-80, long 200-400
- Latency targets: short p95 < 200ms, medium p95 < 800ms, long async throughput target N/A
- Benchmark plan: initial sweep for each model/config (2-4 hrs), steady-state 30-60m per bucket, overnight stress for tails
- Security: customer-managed KMS, SOC2 docs to be shared, VPC peering for Dedicated
- Success criteria: p95 latency targets met, cost per 1k under threshold, correctness on prompt evals within acceptable delta

References shared during call:
- Redwood security packet (link shared in chat)
- Benchmark harness repo (link to be provided by SE)
- Sample prompt set and golden CSV (customer to provide)

End of transcript.
